category_title: Reluctant readers who achieve cognitive flow on digital devices but struggle with print focus
minimal_context: The student is participating in a 50-minute Friday Silent Sustained Reading session in the classroom using a traditional paper book.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for our 50-minute Friday Silent Sustained Reading session. Please open your traditional paper book and begin reading your free choice novel.

STUDENT: I stay more focused when I'm on the Nook.

TUTOR: We are using the paper books right now. Please look at your book and read.

STUDENT: Yeah. I don't know. I just can't focus, can't read.

TUTOR: Just do your best to keep trying for the rest of the period.

STUDENT: I lose focus just randomly. I don't like this because I'm not doing anything but sitting.

options.A: Provide supplemental instruction in academic engagement skills, such as requesting assistance and taking brief breaks.
options.B: Ask follow-up questions about the free choice novel to model conversational skills during the session.
options.C: Involve the student in developing and adjusting an assessment rubric early in the reading unit.
options.D: Provide a wide variety of downloaded books for free choice reading on the e-reader.
